tasks.title: CandyTableDirector robustness: seat mapping, consecutive timeouts, and rejected-action message
tasks.description: Day 7-9. First, SeatOf() maps seats by name with First(s => s.name == p.Name). Duplicate names can link two players to one seat, and a First() failure stops the game coroutine. Replace it with seat-index-based mapping and validate unique names. Second, the timer is only reset on a new turn, so with TimeoutAction = ForcedEat and a good candy, consecutive timeouts happen; reset the timer after the forced action. Third, after a player's action is rejected, the text 'Safe! Keep going…' appears even though nothing was eaten; fix the message.

With TimeoutAction = ForcedEat, timeouts do not happen consecutively within one turn.
Rejected actions do not show the 'Safe! Keep going…' message.
The code compiles, and the scenarios are tested in Play Mode in the Unity Editor with log evidence.

SeatOf() is now seats[p.ConfigIndex] (new PlayerState.ConfigIndex in Core = SeatConfig index before the d20 sort, with an EditMode test); duplicate participant names are reported with a LogWarning during Setup and numbered (e.g. 'Blue 2'). Keep going'. Save the Console log.
